name: Jar wine
summary: Rice or another grain fermented with forest-leaf yeast in a ceramic jar, drunk through bamboo straws. Go Vietnam says it is not distilled. The jar price is not one figure.
origin: Go Vietnam calls rượu cần, also rượu ghè, the jar wine of Xơ Đăng, Ba Na, Gia Rai, Giẻ Triêng, Brâu, and other communities in former Kon Tum.
culture: Go Vietnam says the jar sits at the center of the communal house at festivals. People share straws while gongs play and the xoang is danced. Water is poured in, and the host tops it up after each round.
taste: Go Vietnam’s jar-wine article says a gentle sweetness, a faint bitter edge from the leaf yeast, and the smell of fermented sticky rice. Black sticky rice gives a red or deep-purple liquid. The cluster article says a refreshing sweetness and a Ba Na aroma. The Măng Đen article says Sedang jar wine is more fragrant and lower in alcohol than M’nông jar wine, at 3–7 percent.
howToEat: Sit at one jar. Straws go in. Spring water or cooled boiled water is poured on. Sip in turns. Go Vietnam says the point is sharing, slowly, not finishing the jar. It is a festival and ceremony drink: after harvest, at Tết, at new-rice meals, at a new communal house, and at life-cycle rites. It is not described as the market breakfast.

Prices, not averaged. The cluster article prints 100,000–200,000 VND for a 5-litre jar of Khẩu Cẩm rice wine fermented 6–12 months, with 8–10 straws, in a 10–15 litre jar. The jar-wine article prints about 175,000 VND for a 4-litre container from one maker. The Măng Đen article prints 350,000–600,000 VND for a Sedang jar serving 6–10 people. Check on arrival.
where: Communal houses and festivals in former Kon Tum, and district markets and ethnic women’s workshops on the jar-wine article. A single downtown bar was not named. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Jar wine in Kon Tum — ruou can through straws
seoDescription: Undistilled jar wine of the Xơ Đăng, Ba Na, and neighboring peoples, sipped through straws. Go Vietnam prints 100,000–200,000, about 175,000, and 350,000–600,000 VND.
